title: DVR extension in a quasi-projective ambient gives a projective birational closure
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian integral scheme with function field $K$ and generic point $\eta$. Let $H\to S$ be H-projective and of finite type, let $M\subset H$ be an open subscheme, and let $m:\operatorname{Spec}K\to M$ lie over $\eta$. Let $i:R\hookrightarrow M$ be the reduced closure of $m$, and write $f:R\to S$ for its structure map. Assume $R$ is integral, $f$ is separated, of finite type and locally of finite presentation, and $R_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ with the identification induced by $m$. Suppose that for every discrete valuation subring $A\subset K$ with fraction field $K$ and every $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ whose generic restriction is the generic inclusion of $S$, there is an $S$-morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to M$ restricting to $m$. Then each such $v$ factors uniquely through $i$; $f$ is proper; the composite $R\hookrightarrow M\hookrightarrow H$ is a closed immersion; and $f$ is H-projective and is an isomorphism over a dense open subscheme of $S$. This statement has no curve, normality, Hom-representability or rational-curve hypothesis.

Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Integrality, function fields, H-projectivity, finite type, finite presentation, properness and separatedness, open and closed immersions, discrete valuation rings, spectra and reduction are [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sc-function-field], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Reduced closure means the closure of the image point endowed with reduced induced closed subscheme structure. Dense means that the topological closure is all of $S$.

source.place: Tag 0208 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper), equivalence (1) and (4); de Jong Claim 3.10 and sections 3.11--3.12, printed p.609. Agent-formulated closure criterion, including scheme-theoretic factorization of lifts and the dense-base-open conclusion. The spreading input is the existing lem-sbc-generic-fibre-iso-spread-base-open.

proof.text: Write $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to R$ for the factor of $m$ supplied by the assumed identification $R_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its image $\xi$ is the generic point of $R$: under the closed embedding $i$, its closure is all of $R$ by the definition of reduced closure. On affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset S$ of $\xi,\eta$, integrality makes $B,C$ domains. The generic-fibre identification says $(C\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B=K$, compatibly with $\operatorname{Frac}C=K$. Thus $B\subset K$ and $\operatorname{Frac}B=K$; the induced generic local-ring map is the identity $K\to K$. Consequently $a$ is the canonical generic-point morphism, and $f$ is birational.

source.place: Tag 0208 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper), identification of the canonical generic point; elementary localization using the assumed generic fibre

proof.text: Fix a pair $(A,b)$ in the hypothesis and its lift $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to M$. A DVR is a valuation domain with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Apply [lemma-nagata-valuation-factor-closed] to $i:R\hookrightarrow M$, $v$ and its generic factor $a$ to obtain $w:\operatorname{Spec}A\to R$ with $iw=v$. This factorization is unique: on each affine open of $M$, maps through the quotient ring defining $i$ are uniquely determined by their composite with the quotient map [def-weil-closed-immersion]; these unique maps agree on overlaps. The equality $fw=b$ follows because $v$ is over $S$. Also $w|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=a$ by the same uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 0208 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper), condition (4); scheme-theoretic factorization through a closed subscheme over a domain

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-generic-dvr-properness-criterion] to $f:R\to S$. The base is locally Noetherian, $R$ is integral, and $f$ is separated and finite type by assumption. Step 1 identifies its function field and canonical generic map with $K,a$, so the DVR subrings and base maps required by that criterion are exactly those in the hypothesis. Step 2 supplies all the required extensions. Therefore $f$ is proper.

Put $j:R\hookrightarrow M\hookrightarrow H$ and $q:H\to S$. The given factorization makes $j$ an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Since $q$ is H-projective, [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] makes it proper, hence separated. As $qj=f$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] gives properness of $j$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] now makes $j$ a closed immersion.

Choose the closed embedding $e:H\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ from H-projectivity [def-kun-projective]. The composite $ej:R\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], and its structural composite is $f$. This is precisely H-projectivity of $f$.

Both $R$ and $S$ are integral, so each has just one irreducible component. Step 1 identifies the generic points and their local rings compatibly with $f$. The separated and locally-finite-presentation hypotheses on $f$ are given. Thus [lem-sfb-birational-isomorphism-dense-open] supplies a dense open $U\subseteq S$ with $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism. This proves the last clause without assuming that $R$ is affine.
